title: Dominic, again
tomorrow: how did a wounded soldier find God in his own daydreams?

cards: Some of the most honest conversations happen after midnight, when an argument wears out and turns into actual talking. Here's one. A traveling priest named Dominic stops at an inn in Toulouse, in the south of France.

The innkeeper holds to a teaching the Church considers false. Dominic could eat, sleep and leave in the morning. Instead, says Jordan of Saxony, who knew him, Dominic sits up with the man the whole night, talking.
By morning, the innkeeper has come back to the faith.

teach.h: HE SAT AT THE MAN'S TABLE.
teach.b: Why stay up? Because Dominic thought truth was worth a night's sleep, and a person was worth more. He didn't preach at the man from a pulpit.
He sat at his table. That night became a pattern.
Dominic gathered companions who would study, pray and then go out and talk, and the Church approved them as the Order of Preachers. Their motto is one Latin word: veritas, truth.
Thomas Aquinas, himself a Dominican, put their whole life into one line: to contemplate, and to hand on to others what you've contemplated.
Contemplate and share. Not share first and think later. Not contemplate and keep it to yourself.

teach.h: THE TRUTH SHALL MAKE YOU FREE.
teach.b: Jesus says in John's Gospel, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free."
Here's the one to tell a friend: Jordan remembers Dominic as the best of company by day, cheerful with his brothers, and by night given over to prayer.

The contemplating happened in the dark; the sharing happened at the table. Truth, for Dominic, was never a weapon. It was something you'd stay up all night to share, because the person across the table was worth it.

how: Dominican friars and sisters, the Order of Preachers, take veritas as their motto; they study, pray the Liturgy of the Hours together, and preach and teach. Many Catholics also pray the rosary, a devotion tradition links to Dominic.

practice: Write one true thing you've learned on this whole climb, in a sentence short enough to fit in a text. Read it back slowly, twice, and let it settle.
If you pray, you can ask to share it gently with whoever needs it; if not, just keep the sentence close.
